_about: Genre configurations for Spectre. One entry per genre; `studio.py master --genre <name>` takes the target curve and the mastering settings from `master` (explicit flags override). Every value names its source in the genre doc (`doc`) or below; `hand_tuned` lists values that have no published source yet. There is no default genre. Since 2026-11-25 each genre (except `trap`, the preserved first-release configuration) has an era-appropriate target from engine/targets.json, with its provenance (`target_source`, `target_era`, `target_tracks`, `target_method`, `target_date`); `master_published` keeps the settings the genre's released tracks were mastered with (`master --published`).

trap.name: Trap / beats (the configuration of the first releases of 001-006; 808-driven: trap, drill, rage, folk-fusion trap; boom-bap is sample-driven and has `boombap` and `hiphop_golden`)
trap.status: the configuration of the first releases of sessions 001-006, preserved exactly (the former engine default; `--target beat` is an alias; add `--legacy-master` to reproduce those masters). Sessions 001-006 were remastered with `hiphop` on 2026-11-24
trap.form: an intro, a real arrangement (hooks and verses) and an outro
trap.tempo: 130-160 bpm with a half-time feel (65-80 felt); sessions 001-006 ran 136-160
trap.role: it should feel like a real beat an artist could rap on
hand_tuned: target curve `beat` (808 sub-forward; not measured from references)
translate 0.5
eq 0.7
sources: length: Billboard Hot 100 top-10 hip-hop hits averaged 2:48 in 2019 (Billboard, https://www.billboard.com/?p=8514407, not re-verified 2026-11: page unreachable); Spotify charting songs averaged about 3:00 in 2024, hip-hop -29 s since 2018 (Chartmetric, https://hmc.chartmetric.com/shorter-songs-trend-streaming-history/)

loudness: 54 Billboard Global 200 top-10 songs (H1 2024) averaged -8.3 LUFS integrated, sd 1 LU (iZotope, https://www.izotope.com/en/learn/mastering-trends); -10.5 is an engine-limited choice (the true-peak guard stops gaining past about -9.5), streaming normalizes to -14 (Spotify)

joc.form: rounds of a dance tune: strains of 8 or 16 bars of 2/4, each repeated with variation, faster each round; an optional slow (rar) opening, then the fast (repede) dance, an accelerating last round and a stop; primas preludes and interludes
joc.tempo: dance tempo quarter = 110-140 in 2/4; a slow rar or listening section can sit far lower (the reference score's practice ladder runs 50, 70, 90, 110); tempo rises round by round and accelerates at the end (section bpm ramps)
joc.meter: 2/4: bass on the beats, chords on the afterbeats; one engine pattern bar = two bars of 2/4
joc.change_rate: something changes every strain (8-16 bars of 2/4 = 4-8 pattern bars); the tempo steps up each round
joc.role: the violin leads throughout (melody, preludes, interludes, improvisation); guitar and bass hold the afterbeat (tiitura); percussion carries the dancers; a voice is optional (shouts to the dancers)
hand_tuned: translate 0.3
change_rate (derived from the dance form; the exact rate is craft)

form and tempo: the reference score's four passes at quarter = 50/70/90/110; Dans Tiganesc Rar (6/8) then Repede (2/4) (https://socalfolkdance.org/dances/D/Dans_Tiganesc_Rar-Dans_Tignanesc_Repede.pdf); slow-medium-fast-faster order and accelerations (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gypsy_style); AcousticBrainz tempo estimates 94-172 bpm

role: the primas leads (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanian_folk_violin); a wedding band with violin, guitar, string bass, accordions, cimbalom and a vocalist (Beissinger 2007, https://journals.ku.edu/folklorica/article/view/3757)

caroling.length: 2:00-3:30, typically 2:20-3:15 (one carol, a few verses; medleys and concert anthems run longer)
caroling.form: strophic: verses of 4 or 8 phrases (each 2 or 4 bars) with a refrain or chorus; 2-4 verses; variation by texture between verses (unison, harmony, a descant, a key lift, a bells or brass interlude), an intro of the last phrase or a bell peal, a held or ritardando ending
caroling.tempo: felt pulse about 50-60 per dotted quarter in 6/8 carols, quarter = 84-112 in duple and triple carols; slow carols lower; rubato and a final ritardando
caroling.meter: 3/4, 6/8 or 4/4; no backbeat; a 3-beat carol bar = 12 steps (4 carol bars = 3 engine bars)
caroling.change_rate: by verse and phrase: something changes every verse (4-8 carol bars), dynamics and texture inside a verse follow the words
caroling.role: the carolers carry the tune as a choir texture (voices as instruments: wordless or short refrain fragments, a call at the door); bells, brass and organ answer and fill; no lead vocal carrying verses
hand_tuned: lufs -14: a choice between the Holiday 100 average (-12.9) and choral albums (about -19 to -23, estimated)
translate 0.2: little bass-harmonic enhancement (no bass instrument leads)
change_rate (craft, from the strophic form)
eq 0.3: the era assessment's recommendation for a loose reference curve (docs/CAROLING.md)
max_low_boost_db 0: no low-end boosts (clean-up and a ceiling only), the era assessment's recommendation

chamberscore.change_rate: by phrase and period: something changes every 8-16 bars (the theme moves to another instrument, a layer joins or leaves); the big changes are tempo, density and dynamics
chamberscore.role: a piano or a whimsical lead (glockenspiel, celesta, whistle, violin, clarinet-like reed) carries the theme; the accompaniment (waltz bass and chords, pizzicato, guitar or ukulele strums) leaves the middle for it; a voice, if any, is an instrument (a wordless line, a hum, a children's-choir colour)

techno.form: a DJ tool: intro 16-32 bars of kick (and rumble) only; a main section 32-64 bars that adds bass, the hook sound and percussion layer by layer; a breakdown 16-32 bars without the kick (0-8 in hypnotic and minimal strands); a re-entry and peak 32-64 bars; an outro 16-32 bars back to kick and percussion; an element in or out about every 16 bars over an 8-bar loop; builds by filters, density and layers rather than silence and drops
techno.tempo: by strand: 124-128 melodic, dub, minimal; 130-140 peak-time / driving, hypnotic, industrial, hard groove; 145-155 hard techno (peak-time festival 150-155); over 160 is hardstyle, hardcore, hardtekk. Mixgraph techno median 133 (128-140; yearly median 128 in 1991 to 140 in 2025, lowest 126 in 2013); hard techno median 146 (136-155); catalogue (Essentia) 132 in the 1990s, 136 in 2000-08, 126-127 in 2009-18, 130 in 2019-21
techno.meter: 4/4, kick on every quarter (never half time); offbeat open hat, bass or ride; 16th hats; swing 50-54% on hats and percussion only (Attack); swung and syncopated in hard groove and Detroit, straight in hard techno and industrial
techno.change_rate: an element in or out about every 16 bars (8 in the busy strands); slow movement inside sections (filter, resonance, decay, sends over 8-16 bars); the kick leaves only for the breakdown
techno.role: the kick and its low end are the lead; one repeating hook sound (an acid line, a stab, a riff of one or two notes, a loop) over percussion; voices as short loops, shouts or chopped phrases
hand_tuned: lufs -9.5 and the strand levels (-8 hard (tested in the engine 2026-11-26), -9 industrial, -9.5 hypnotic, -10.5 minimal, -11 melodic and minimal era, -12 dub, -13 roots): choices against the measured loud sections (Mixgraph previews) and whole tracks (catalogue); untested in the engine
eq 0.7 and translate 0.4 (as trance and dubstep)
max_low_boost_db 2 (the heaviest measured low end in the project: the mix must supply 50-80 Hz)

psytrance.form: DJ intro 32-64 bars (kick and bass from bar 1 or 17), drive 32-64, short break 8-16 (kick and bass rest), drive, the big breakdown about two-thirds in (up to 64 bars) with the theme, build 8-32, a 4-beat pause (the cliff), main drop 32-64 in 16-bar blocks with 4-beat gaps, DJ outro 32 (down to kick and bass); two or three drops

psytrance.change_rate: add or remove an element every 4 or 8 bars; work in 16-bar blocks
psytrance.role: kick and bass are the record; leads, acid lines and FX answer each other above them; samples or a gated voice instead of a singer
